guide.summary: Saul was persecuting Christians when Jesus encountered him on the Damascus road. Transformed into apostle Paul, he traveled throughout the Greco-Roman world founding churches. His letters continue to guide Christian faith today.

keyVerses.text: Go, because this man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles.
But I do not account my life of any value, if only I may finish my course.
The God who made the world does not dwell in temples built by human hands.

exercises.prompt: What was Saul doing when Jesus encountered him?
exercises.text: Saul had a purpose that would be transformed.
options: Persecuting Christians on the way to Damascus
Teaching the law of the Pharisees
exercises.answer: Persecuting Christians on the way to Damascus
exercises.explanation: Saul was zealously fighting against the Church when his encounter with Jesus changed everything.

exercises.statement: Jesus personally appeared to Saul on the Damascus road.
exercises.explanation: The risen Jesus Himself appeared to Saul, asking why he persecuted Him.

exercises.prompt: What was the first consequence of the vision?
exercises.text: The transformation began with a loss followed by recovery.
options: Saul was blinded and his sight was restored
Saul fell from his horse and was injured
exercises.answer: Saul was blinded and his sight was restored
exercises.explanation: Saul's blindness was symbolic: he needed to be restored spiritually.

exercises.text: Paul's calling in Acts 9:15
This is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name.
options: Paul will be a great apostle

exercises.text: "This is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the _____.

exercises.statement: Paul's conversion was merely an event with no lasting change.
exercises.explanation: Paul spent the rest of his life dedicated to Jesus and the gospel.

exercises.prompt: What was Paul's method on his journeys?
exercises.text: Paul had a clear strategy for evangelizing.
options: Going to Jewish synagogues and then to the Gentiles
exercises.answer: Going to Jewish synagogues and then to the Gentiles
exercises.explanation: Paul always started in synagogues, presenting Jesus first to the Jews.

exercises.statement: Paul traveled alone on his missions.
exercises.explanation: Paul had companions like Barnabas, Silas and Timothy on his journeys.

exercises.prompt: What did Paul face during his travels?
exercises.text: Paul's journeys were marked by continuous persecution.
exercises.explanation: Paul suffered greatly for the gospel, but never gave up.

exercises.text: Paul's commitment in Acts 20:24
My life is not of value to me.
"If only I may finish my _____."

exercises.statement: Paul established churches in multiple regions during his travels.
exercises.explanation: Paul founded churches in Antioch, Corinth, Ephesus and many other places.

exercises.prompt: Where did Paul deliver his famous speech?
exercises.text: A city known for philosophy and multiple gods.
exercises.explanation: Athens was an intellectual center where Paul confronted pagan philosophies.

exercises.statement: Paul recognized the altar to the unknown god in Athens.
exercises.explanation: Paul used this altar as a starting point to preach about Jesus.

exercises.prompt: What was the central message of the speech at the Areopagus?
exercises.text: Paul presented truths about God to the Greeks.
options: God does not dwell in temples made with human hands
The idols are superior to God
exercises.answer: God does not dwell in temples made with human hands
exercises.explanation: Paul confronted polytheism with the truth about the one true God.

exercises.text: Truth about God in Acts 17:24-25
tokens: The God who made the world
nor is he served by human hands
distractors: to all mankind life and breath

exercises.text: The God who made the world does not dwell in temples.
"The God who made the world does not dwell in ___ made with hands."

exercises.statement: Everyone in Athens immediately accepted Paul's message.
exercises.explanation: Some mocked, but others believed and joined Paul.

exercises.prompt: How was Paul brought to Rome?
exercises.text: A dramatic journey marked the end of Acts.
options: As a prisoner under Roman guard
exercises.answer: As a prisoner under Roman guard
exercises.explanation: Paul was imprisoned, tried and sent to Rome to appeal to Caesar.

exercises.statement: During the journey to Rome, Paul faced a shipwreck.
exercises.explanation: A ship on which Paul was traveling was wrecked during a storm.

exercises.prompt: What was Paul's hope while imprisoned?
exercises.text: Paul maintained a faithful stance even while in prison.
options: To testify in Rome and be with Jesus
exercises.answer: To testify in Rome and be with Jesus
exercises.explanation: Paul spent two years in Rome preaching and teaching about Jesus.

exercises.text: The final journey in Acts 27:23-24
tokens: I belong and whom I serve
distractors: and said Do not be afraid

exercises.text: An angel of the God whom I serve stood by me.
"It is necessary that you appear before _____.

exercises.statement: Paul's imprisonment interrupted his preaching ministry.
exercises.explanation: Paul continued preaching even in prison, showing that nothing can silence the gospel.

exercises.text: A radical transformation began on the Damascus road.
options: Through a personal encounter on the road
exercises.answer: Through a personal encounter on the road
exercises.explanation: Jesus personally appeared to Saul, transforming him instantly.

exercises.statement: Paul faced difficulties in sharing the gospel.
exercises.explanation: Paul experienced rejection, persecution and imprisonment, but never gave up.

exercises.prompt: What was God's purpose for Paul?
exercises.text: God had a specific plan for this apostle.
options: To be a chosen instrument to proclaim the gospel to the Gentiles
To be priest of the temple
exercises.answer: To be a chosen instrument to proclaim the gospel to the Gentiles
exercises.explanation: Paul was specially called to reach the Gentiles with the gospel.

exercises.statement: Paul's life demonstrates that God can transform anyone.
exercises.explanation: Paul is the greatest example of transformation and dedication to Jesus in the Bible.
